title: Weather and Climate
summary: The difference between weather and climate, elements of weather and how they are measured, factors that influence climate, and reading climate graphs.

notes.text: The condition of the atmosphere at a particular place and time, for example 'hot and windy in Bloemfontein today'. Weather changes from day to day.
The average weather conditions of a place measured over a long period, usually at least 30 years, for example 'Cape Town has hot, dry summers and cool, wet winters'.

rows: Compass direction the wind blows FROM

notes.label: Remember
notes.text: Winds are named after the direction they blow **from**. A south-easter blows from the south-east.

rows: Places near the equator receive direct sunlight and are hot; places near the poles are cold
Lagos is hotter than Cape Town
Temperature falls about 6,5 °C for every 1 000 m of height
Johannesburg (1 750 m) is cooler than Durban at the same season
The sea heats and cools slowly, so coastal places have a mild climate; inland places have extreme temperatures (hot days, cold nights)
Warm currents bring warm, moist air and rain; cold currents cool the air and cause dry conditions
Warm Agulhas Current (east coast), cold Benguela Current (west coast)
Moist air rises over mountains, cools and drops rain on the windward side; the leeward side is dry (rain shadow)
The Drakensberg: wet on the KZN side, drier in Lesotho's interior
Winds from the sea bring moisture; winds from the land are dry

items: **Convection rain**: the ground heats the air, which rises, cools and forms thunderclouds; common in summer on the Highveld (afternoon thunderstorms).
**Relief (orographic) rain**: moist air is forced up over mountains and cools.
**Frontal (cyclonic) rain**: warm and cold air masses meet, the warm air rises; brings winter rain to the Western Cape.

notes.title: Rain on the Drakensberg
notes.problem: Moist air from the Indian Ocean blows towards the Drakensberg. Why is the east side wet and the west side dry?
steps: The air is forced upward when it meets the mountains, and it cools.
Water vapour condenses and rain falls on the east, the windward side.
The air then sinks on the west, the leeward side, where it warms and dries.
notes.answer: This is relief rainfall, and the dry side is in a rain shadow.

notes.text: A **climate graph** shows average monthly **temperature** as a line graph and average monthly **rainfall** as a bar graph, on the same set of axes.

notes.title: Calculating from climate data
notes.problem: A town's highest monthly average temperature is 26 °C (January) and lowest is 12 °C (July). Calculate the annual temperature range.

notes.label: Exam tip
notes.text: In the southern hemisphere, summer is December to February and winter is June to August. If most rain falls in June to August, the place has **winter rainfall**.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between weather and climate?
questions.memo:
✓ Weather is the condition of the atmosphere at a particular time (day to day) (1)
✓ Climate is the average weather over a long period, usually 30 years (1)

questions.prompt: A south-easter is a wind that blows towards the south-east.
questions.explanation: Winds are named after the direction they blow from.

questions.prompt: Why is Johannesburg cooler than Durban?
options: It is closer to the equator
It is at a higher altitude
It is near a cold current

questions.prompt: The hottest month in a town averages 31 °C and the coldest 9 °C. What is the annual temperature range?
Match each instrument to what it measures.
Explain why the east coast of South Africa is wetter than the west coast.
questions.memo:
✓ The warm Agulhas Current flows along the east coast; the cold Benguela Current along the west coast (1)
✓ Warm water heats the air above it, which holds more moisture and brings rain (1)
✓ Cold water cools the air, so it holds little moisture and the west is dry (1)

✓ The dry area on the leeward side of a mountain (1)
✓ because the air has already lost its moisture as rain on the windward side and descends dry (1)
